assumptions: Both melting temperatures are primer3 thal's nearest-neighbour values at the stated salt and oligo conditions.
limits: The default margin is a design tool's rule of thumb with no primary citation; the verdict is only as good as the margin passed.
Says nothing about the blocker or the primer's own priming.
bio.jane/contract.noReading: The Design tab's Scorpion section shows the two temperatures, the difference and the margin flag with whose rule it is; it writes no sentence over them, and the door returns the same fields.
bio.jane/contract.question: Does a Scorpion probe's stem melt below the loop-target duplex by the margin the design needs?

description: A Scorpion probe's two melting temperatures, side by side: the stem-loop's own hairpin and the duplex the loop makes with its target on the amplicon. A Scorpion is a primer carrying a stem-loop probe on a non-amplifiable blocker (Whitcombe 1999), and it reports by the loop finding its target and pulling the stem apart - so the design question is a RELATION between those two structures, not a property of either. Returns both temperatures, their difference, the stem's GC, and a verdict against WHATEVER margin you pass. It does not apply a margin of its own authority: the widely-quoted 5-10 °C figure comes from one design tool's tech note and has no primary citation, so the default is labelled as that rule of thumb and every result says which margin produced its verdict.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

conditions.description: salt, magnesium, dNTP and oligo concentrations plus the salt-correction method the stem Tm is measured in. Left unset it is filled from your reaction-conditions settings, and falls back to primer3's defaults when there are none. Advanced.

additives.description: DMSO and formamide, applied AFTER the nearest-neighbour Tm.

DMSOfactor.description: °C of Tm lost per % DMSO, as an explicit override. Supplying it WINS over `dmsoMethod`, and detaches the number from its citation.

dmsoMethod.description: which published DMSO depression sets the coefficient. Values: ahs01 (Ahsen et al. (2001) (0.75 °C per %)), mus81 (Musielski et al. (1981) (0.6 °C per %)), cul76 (Cullen and Bick (1976) (0.5 °C per %)), esc80 (Escara and Hutton (1980) (0.675 °C per %)).

fmd.description: formamide — percent when `fmdmethod` is 1, molar when it is 2.

fmdfactor.description: °C lost per % formamide (method 1). Papers report 0.6 to 0.72.

fmdmethod.description: 1 = linear % formamide (McConaughy 1969) · 2 = GC-dependent, molar (Blake & Delcourt 1996). Values: 1 (Linear %, McConaughy 1969), 2 (GC-dependent molar, Blake & Delcourt 1996).

method.description: which validated nearest-neighbour model and default buffer — santaLucia (pydna `tm_default`, Taq) or dbd (pydna `tm_dbd`, Phusion / Pfu-Sso7d). Values: santaLucia (SantaLucia (pydna tm_default, Taq)), dbd (DNA-binding domain (pydna tm_dbd, Phusion)).

nnTable.description: override the method's nearest-neighbour table; the buffer convention is unchanged.

saltcorr.description: Biopython salt-correction method 0–7 (0 = none). It moves the answer more than any other knob here: on a 24-mer at the Taq buffer the eight span 79.302 °C (method 0) to 66.009 °C (method 2).

selfcomp.description: both strands are one self-complementary oligo (the concentration term becomes dnac1 rather than dnac1 − dnac2/2).

margin.description: how many °C the stem Tm must exceed the loop-target Tm for the verdict to pass. Yours to set: the 5-10 °C rule of thumb this defaults to the floor of is a design tool's, not a measured value from the primary literature. In °C.

probe.description: the whole probe element, 5' stem arm + loop + 3' stem arm. The element is what folds, so it is what the structure engine is given - the loop alone would compute a hairpin the molecule does not have.

stem_length.description: how many bases of the 5' end form the stem arm. Reported back rather than guessed. The two vendors disagree on the range - LGC Biosearch, who sell Scorpions, publish 5-7 nt and PremierBiosoft's design tool says 6-7 - so neither is enforced. In nt.

target.description: the loop's target on the amplicon, 5'->3'. This is the OTHER temperature: a Scorpion opens because the loop finds this, so it is the loop-target duplex that has to be stable, not the loop's own self-structure.

name: check_scorpion_stem

clearsMargin.description: whether the difference clears the margin GIVEN - null when either temperature could not be computed

difference.description: stemTm - probeTm, the quantity the design rule is about

marginSource.description: where the margin came from, carried with the verdict so an unsourced rule of thumb is never mistaken for a measurement

notes.description: why a temperature is missing, in the words the panel shows. Empty when both were computed

probeTm.description: melting temperature of the loop-target duplex, °C

stemGcPercent.description: GC of the 5' stem arm - both vendors ask for a GC-rich stem

stemTm.description: melting temperature of the probe element's own hairpin, °C - null when no stem forms
